questions.question: Which among the following is an idiom?
questions.solution: Question 1: Which among the following is an idiom? The correct answer is **Option (4)** i.e. **Water under the bridge**. **__Key Points__** __ • The word **idiom** refers to a set expression or a phrase comprising two or more words that has a specific meaning which is different from the literal meaning of its individual components. questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'top banana'?

options.text: A person whose hands are very thin
A beggar or a very poor person

(**प्रमुख व्यक्ति**) • **Example:** In that law firm, she is the **top banana** and has the final word on all legal strategies. • **'A leader, boss, chief person in a group'** describes someone who holds the highest rank or authority within a specific set of people. (**एक समूह का नेता, बॉस, या मुख्य व्यक्ति**) • **Example:** After years of hard work, he finally became the **top banana** of the engineering team. • Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom **'top banana'** is **'a leader, boss, chief person in a group'**. Therefore, the correct answer is: **A leader, boss, chief person in a group**. **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings: • **A person whose hands are very thin** (**एक व्यक्ति जिसके हाथ बहुत पतले हैं**): This is a literal physical description and does not carry an idiomatic meaning in this context. • **A beggar or a very poor person** (**एक भिखारी या बहुत गरीब व्यक्ति**): This refers to someone in extreme poverty; common idioms for this include 'church mouse' or 'down-and-out'. • **A person whose neck is long** (**एक व्यक्ति जिसकी गर्दन लंबी है**): This is a physical observation and is not related to the meaning of 'top banana'. 36:Tb0a, The correct answer is **Option (2)** i.e. **significant**.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Did the magician perform amazing tricks at the fair?

options.text: Were amazing tricks performed at the fair by the magician?
Have amazing tricks been performed at the fair by the magician?
Are amazing tricks performed at the fair by the magician?
Will amazing tricks be performed at the fair by the magician?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Were amazing tricks performed at the fair by the magician?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is an **Interrogative Sentence** in the **Simple Past Tense**, as indicated by the auxiliary verb **Did** followed by the base form of the verb **perform**.

• In the **Active Voice**, the structure of a **Simple Past** question is: **Did + Subject + V1 (Base Verb) + Object**. Here, the **Subject** is **the magician** and the **Object** is **amazing tricks**.

• To transform this into **Passive Voice**, the **Object** (amazing tricks) of the active sentence becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence.

• The structure for **Passive Voice** in **Simple Past Interrogative** is: **Was/Were + New Subject + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Agent**.

• Since the new subject **amazing tricks** is **plural**, the correct auxiliary verb to be used at the beginning of the sentence is **Were**.

• The main verb **perform** must be changed to its **Past Participle** form, which is **performed**.

• The phrase **at the fair** is an **adverbial adjunct** and remains in its relative position, while the agent **the magician** is introduced using the preposition **by**.

 **Additional Information__**

• Comparison with incorrect options based on **Tense** and **Aspect**:

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Option 2 uses **Have... been performed**. This structure is used only if the active sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense** (e.g., Has the magician performed...).

• **Simple Present Passive**: Option 3 uses **Are... performed**. This is used for habitual actions or general truths in the **Simple Present Tense** (e.g., Does the magician perform...).

• **Simple Future Passive**: Option 4 uses **Will... be performed**. This is reserved for actions that have not yet occurred, corresponding to the **Simple Future Tense** (e.g., Will the magician perform...).

• **Number Agreement**: In passive constructions, the verb must always agree with the **new subject**. If the object were singular (e.g., an amazing trick), the auxiliary **Was** would have been used instead of **Were**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Will the infrastructure projects have been completed by the government before the deadline set by the council?

options.text: Will the government complete the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?
Will the government have completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?
Will have the government completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?
Will the government completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the government have completed the infrastructure projects before the deadline set by the council?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Future Perfect Tense**, indicated by the construction **will + object + have been + past participle (completed)**.
 
• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice in the **Future Perfect Tense**, the structure must follow: **Will + Subject + have + Past Participle (V3) + Object?**
 
• In the passive sentence, **the government** is the agent (doer), and **the infrastructure projects** is the patient (receiver). In the active voice, **the government** shifts to the **subject** position.
 
• The auxiliary verb **will** remains at the start to maintain the **interrogative form**, followed immediately by the new subject.
 
• The phrase **before the deadline set by the council** is an **adverbial modifier** that provides temporal context and remains unchanged in its position at the end of the sentence.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Perfect Tense**:
 
 
• It denotes an action that will be **completed** between now and a specific point in the future.
 
• In **Active Voice**, the helping verbs are **will have** followed by the **third form of the verb**.
 
 
 
• **Common Structural Errors**:
 
 
• **Future Simple**: Using **will complete** (as seen in Option 1) changes the aspect of the verb from perfect to simple.
 
• **Syntax Errors**: Placing the auxiliary **have** before the subject (as in Option 3) creates an **incorrect interrogative structure** in English.
 
• **Morphological Errors**: Using **will** directly with **completed** (as in Option 4) without **have** is grammatically invalid.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
Each of the representatives from the various states have presented their reports on healthcare reforms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary grammatical issue in the sentence is the **Subject-Verb Agreement**.
 
• The subject of the sentence is '**Each**', which is a **singular distributive pronoun**.
 
• In English grammar, when '**Each of**' is followed by a plural noun (in this case, 'representatives'), the **verb** must always remain **singular**.
 
• The original sentence incorrectly uses the plural verb '**have presented**'. To make it grammatically correct, it must be replaced by the singular verb '**has presented**'.
 
• While traditional grammar often preferred 'his or her' with 'each', modern usage commonly accepts '**their**' as a singular gender-neutral pronoun, making **Option 2** the most suitable choice among the given alternatives.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'Each of the representatives from the various states **has presented their reports** on healthcare reforms.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** '**have presented their report**' – This is incorrect because it retains the plural verb '**have**'.
 
• **Option 3:** '**were presented their reports**' – This is incorrect because '**were**' is a plural verb and the passive construction changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** '**No improvement required**' – This is incorrect because the original sentence contains a clear **subject-verb agreement error** where a plural verb is used for a singular subject.

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. One day, as he was walking about beneath the tree, he saw several young snakes coming out of a hole in the ground. 

A. I left you starving, and now here you are, well and strong!" 

B. When they grew strong and began to move about in the jungle, they met their mother, who exclaimed: "I can't believe it! 

C. The herdsman felt sorry for them, so every day he gave them some milk. D. They looked thin and miserable. 

S2. They told her how the herdsman had taken care of them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows a chronological and logical sequence describing an encounter between a **herdsman**, some **young snakes**, and their **mother**.
 
• **Sentence S1** sets the scene where a person sees **young snakes** coming out of a hole.
 
• **Sentence D follows S1** as it describes the condition of the snakes mentioned in the first sentence:
 
 
• 'They looked **thin and miserable**.'
 
 
 
• **Sentence C follows D** as it explains the herdsman's compassionate response to their poor condition:
 
 
• 'The **herdsman** felt sorry for them, so every day he gave them some **milk**.'
 
 
 
• **Sentence B follows C**, showing the result of the feeding and introducing a new character:
 
 
• 'When they **grew strong** and began to move about in the jungle, they met their **mother**, who exclaimed: 'I can't believe it!'
 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows B** as it completes the mother's dialogue expressing her shock:
 
 
• 'I left you **starving**, and now here you are, **well and strong**!'
 
 
 
• Finally, **Sentence S2** concludes the narrative by explaining that the snakes told their mother about the **herdsman's care**.
 
• The correct logical sequence is **DCBA**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'One day, as he was walking about beneath the tree, he saw several **young snakes** coming out of a hole in the ground. They looked **thin and miserable**. The **herdsman** felt sorry for them, so every day he gave them some **milk**. When they **grew strong** and began to move about in the jungle, they met their **mother**, who exclaimed: 'I can't believe it! I left you **starving**, and now here you are, **well and strong**!' They told her how the herdsman had **taken care** of them.'</div

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
She didn't study for the test, so she was unable to answer most of the questions.

options.text: She didn't studied for the test
She don't study for the test
She doesn't study for the test

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part of the sentence is **grammatically correct** and does not require any changes.
 
• The sentence is set in the **past tense**, as indicated by the phrase **was unable** in the second clause.
 
• In the **simple past tense** (negative), the structure used is **subject + did not (didn't) + base form of the verb**.
 
• The phrase **didn't study** correctly follows this rule, where **didn't** is the auxiliary verb and **study** is the base form (V1).
 
• Therefore, the sentence is **consistent in tense** and logically sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is **No improvement required**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'She **didn't study for the test**, so she was unable to answer most of the questions.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** 'She **didn't studied**' is incorrect because the auxiliary verb **did** is already in the past tense; the main verb must remain in its **base form**.
 
• **Option 2:** 'She **don't study**' is incorrect because **don't** is used with plural subjects (and I/you), while **She** is third-person singular. Furthermore, it is in the **present tense**.
 
• **Option 3:** 'She **doesn't study**' is grammatically correct as a standalone phrase in the **present tense**, but it creates a **tense mismatch** with the rest of the sentence (was unable).
</ul
